text:
nina: Noticing repeated p95 blips in eu-central during the 02:00-03:00 UTC window. Looks like GPU warmers + egress queueing again but with a slightly different fingerprint (PCIe parity warnings on some nodes).

omar: I see it on the topology view. 4 nodes in rack-3 show concurrent NVLink retransmits and uplink queue spikes.

lee: Any persistent tenant ID? shared or dedicated?

nina: Shared tenants. This time it's many small jobs aligning rather than a few big ones.

pat: I grabbed logs for req=txn-warm-074: shows ~110ms added by egress proxy, plus kernel logs with pci_link events.

toni: PromQLs that helped me:  
```
max_over_time(egress_proxy_queue_len{region="eu-central"}[6m]) by (node)
```
and
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_exec_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le,node))
```

omar: Hypothesis: transient KV-cache regen -> bursty PCIe/NVLink traffic -> proxy backpressure -> tail. We need an isolation strategy that doesn't require callers to change immediately.

nina: Agreed. Proposal: spin up ephemeral "ephemeral-warmers" slices (2 GPUs) and surface an in-proxy warmup detector that tags requests mid-flight so SDK header not required. Detector rule: kvcache_miss_rate delta > 25% over 30s AND request_prefix_bytes > 96 -> tag X-Auto-Warm=1.

lee: That detector seems handy but we should canary the tagging in read-only mode first (tag but don't reroute).

pat: Implementation plan: 1) create node label gpu_pool=ephemeral-warmer and AllocationClass ephemeral-warmer-ttl (ttl=10m, preempt=false); 2) add proxy route matcher for header X-Auto-Warm or X-Warmup from SDK; 3) add detector module behind feature flag that can tag requests; 4) egress shaping: fairshare weight 0.2 + token-bucket cap 64KB/s.

omar: Proxy snippet I sketched:  
```
route:
  match: header("X-Auto-Warm") == "1" OR header("X-Warmup") == "1"
  pool: ephemeral-warmer
  pool.qos.weight: 0.2
  pool.egress.limit_bytes_per_sec: 65536
```

toni: Node-level fallback: if pool queue > 80 for >1m, node-agent applies tc tbf rate 64kbps on eth0 to bound uplink while we scale the pool.

lee: Before rolling, run a traffic replay in staging mimicking high kv-miss delta + prefix-gen bursts. We should compare egress p95, NVLink error-rate, and overall token/sec.

nina: I can coordinate staging. Staging cluster "staging-euc-ephemeral" is empty. Omar, can you prepare the AllocationClass and label 3 nodes there?

omar: On it. Creating AllocationClass ephemeral-warmer-ephemeral with selector gpu_pool=ephemeral-warmer.

pat: SRE-bot, please register a temporary alert ephemeral-warmer-pressure (slack-only, 3m burn) so the canary doesn't flip-flop.

sre-bot: Alert created: ephemeral-warmer-pressure (severity: warning) -> paging disabled, slack only.

toni: Replay in staging results: compared to shared baseline, ephemeral-warmer reduced egress p95 by ~50%, NVLink retransmit rate down ~60%. Median unchanged. Token/sec for warmup path decreased ~3% due to shaping.

lee: Cost/infra tradeoff? Reserving tiny silos will increase utilization delta.

omar: Estimated infra cost +2% regionally while trial active. Finance ok for limited trial capped to two racks.

nina: Rollout suggestion: phase 1: detector in tag-only mode for 24h to verify tagging accuracy and false-positive rate. Phase 2: enable routing for 5% of auto-tagged warmups for 1h (canary). Gating metrics: region_egress_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.4 OR nvlink_err_rate > baseline*2 OR ephemeral-warmer_queue_len > 100 for >2m -> immediate rollback.

pat: Also add console metrics: per-pool egress_p95 and per-pool token_rate so PMs and customers can see effect. Add tenant opt-out toggle for the trial.

toni: For SDK change, we'll add X-Warmup header behind an env flag so product teams can opt-in quickly if they prefer caller-side marking. But detector helps with existing clients.

lee: Runbook for oncall: 1) disable ephemeral-warmer route in proxy; 2) scale allocation class to 0; 3) revert detector to tag-only; 4) collect nvlink/pci logs and escalate.

omar: Allocation class and labels created in staging. Replay job uploaded to perf-jobs and results linked.

nina: Great. I'll enable detector in tag-only mode and leave for 24h. If false-positive <2% and metrics look good, proceed to 5% canary.

pat: One extra thought: phase 3 we could implement a predictive warmup schedule (pre-warm KV before predicted peaks) to avoid regen alignment altogether. Longer-term.

nina: Love that. For now, tag-only detector -> 5% canary -> scale if green. Thanks team.
